summary: Monthly company all-hands. Maya opened with a brief company health update (revenue pacing, hiring), product leadership walked through Q1 roadmap priorities (Hosted API enhancements, Dedicated capacity features, Private deployment improvements), infra gave a status on latency/regression work and Dedicated benchmarks, GTM shared enterprise traction and pricing experiments, and People reviewed updated hiring/on-call plans. Meeting closed with Q&A and clear next steps.
transcript: 00:00 Maya: Okay everyone, um, welcome to the January all-hands. Thanks for joining, I know it's a busy week. We'll kick off with a quick company update and then Jae will run through product and roadmap, Rina will do infra, Liam with GTM, and Priya will close with people ops. We'll leave 15 minutes for Q&A. 00:25 Elliot: Quick logistics note — recording is on, captions are on, if you have questions drop them in Q&A or raise your hand. 00:35 Maya: All right, high level — Q4 ended stronger than we modeled, revenue pacing is slightly ahead of plan, we saw a bump from a few mid-market renewals that came through. We are pacing well into Q1, but we still need to be disciplined on hiring and runway. 01:02 Maya: A couple of wins — launched the new streaming improvements in hosted last month, customers reported noticeably lower first-byte times, so nice work there. Also, a shoutout to the SE and solutions team for three POCs that moved to pilot. 01:25 Audience murmur / clapping (inaudible) 01:35 Jae: Thanks Maya. I'll go through the Q1 product priorities. Top 3 focus areas: 1) Improve Hosted API latency and predictable tail latency, 2) Dedicated capacity feature parity and autoscale improvements, 3) Private deployment onboarding and compliance docs. 02:02 Jae: For Hosted we have three sprint goals — smarter routing policies, prefix caching improvements, and a streaming protocol tweak to reduce RTTs. Early bench numbers look promising but we need more real traffic validation. 02:30 Speaker 1 (possible Jae): We will also start a cross-team effort to standardize our model catalog metadata so deployments and customers can pin versions reliably, there's been some confusion with aliasing. 03:00 Elliot: On the infra side Rina and team have been working on kernel selection improvements and quantization testing. Rina, do you want to share the Dedicated benchmark status? 03:15 Rina: Yeah quick update — we ran end-to-end benchmarks on our Dedicated pool last week. Results show a 12-18% improvement in throughput after the kernel changes for the medium-length seqs, tail latencies still need work, especially under spike. We're investigating auto-burst logic to avoid cold-starty drops. 03:40 Rina: One note, transcription: we saw some noisy measurements from an old profiling script, so take the initial numbers with a grain of salt, but directionally good. 04:10 Liam: From GTM — pipeline is healthy, we're seeing more interest from AI-native startups and a couple of enterprise evaluations in finance. Pricing experiment: we're testing usage with committed tier discounts versus simple per-token; early signals show enterprise prefers predictability even at a slightly higher unit cost. 04:45 Liam: Also, we've updated the sales playbook for Dedicated — emphasizing predictable latency and isolation, and we added security talk tracks around KMS/HSM and SOC2 timelines. 05:10 Priya: People update — hiring will be focused and targeted this quarter. We're capping new IC hires to critical roles: infra backend, SEs, and a few product engineers. We'll pause some roles until we see continued revenue lift. Also rolling out a revised on-call rotation to balance load. 05:40 Maya: Quick finance note — burn is within plan given the hires we committed to in December, but we should avoid scope creep. Please work with your managers before pushing new contractor budgets. 06:05 Maya: Okay we'll open up for questions, queue is up. 06:20 Q&A segment begins — various participants ask questions. 06:25 Employee: Hi, question for infra — are the Dedicated improvements compatible with our quantized model flows? 06:32 Rina: Yes, the kernel selector handles float16 and int8 paths, but we did find a perf regression for a specific int8 path on the older driver. We're patching that, ETA early next week. 06:50 Employee: On Hosted routing—any update on customer-configurable fallbacks? 06:55 Jae: We're prototyping a per-tenant routing policy, it'll let SEs set a prioritized fallback list (e.g., cheaper model variants) and maximum acceptable added latency. Planning to roll to a small set of customers for testing mid-Feb. 07:25 Employee: SOC2 status? 07:30 Maya: We're on track for readiness audit in March, evidence collection is 80% complete, and the controls around logging and RBAC are being validated. 07:50 Employee: Any changes to PTO or comp? 07:53 Priya: No changes to PTO. Comp cycles are on the normal annual cadence; we will share details in mid-Feb comp comms. 08:10 Remote side conversation / someone says thanks 08:15 Maya: Quick reminder: if you're running experiments that materially change infra costs, sync with finance. We need to tag those in the cost center. 08:30 Liam: A note on enterprise — for a couple of finance prospects they requested on-prem deployment and audit logs. We already have the Private deployment offering but need to beef up the onboarding docs and a playbook for network setup. 08:55 Jae: We'll prioritize Private deployment quickstart and a hardened checklist for customers — target end of Feb for a first pass. 09:10 Rina: On autoscale — the current policy is reactive and we saw oscillation with short-lived spikes. We're experimenting with a predictive scaler based on sequence length distributions; preliminary model reduces oscillation but increases short-term cost slightly. We'll present options to Eng leadership. 09:45 Maya: OK, final points — focus on delivery and not feature creep, keep hiring lean, prioritize Dedicated tail latency and Private docs. Thank you to everyone for the hard work. 10:05 Maya: We'll post the recording and slides. Please add any follow-up questions to the #all-hands channel. 10:20 Meeting ends with informal chatter and a few people dropping off. 10:30 End of recording.
